newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria February unemployment rises to 13.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria February unemployment rises to 13.7 pct.

text.p: The number of people unemployed in Bulgaria rose to 525,148 or 13.7 percent of the workforce in February from 512,992 in January, a National Labour Exchange (NLE) official said on Tuesday.
"Unemployment rose last month as more people who have been out of work for some time registered with the exchange in search of jobs," a NLE spokeswoman told Reuters.

Under NLE preliminary estimates some 160,000 people are expected to be laid off this year, most of them from state enterprises as Bulgaria moves to closing loss-makers in line with pledges made to international lenders. @
"Unemployment will rise steadily in 1997 due to expected urgent stabilisation measures which include an extensive economic restructuring," the spokeswoman said.

"A total of 700,000 Bulgarians could be out of work by June. A rise in unemployment is inevitable if Bulgaria is to meet its pledges to international lenders to close down loss-making state firms and reduce bureaucracy," she said. @

Bulgaria's interim government and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Monday announced an accord on financial reform and funding worth more than $650 million to stabilise the shattered economy over the next year. @

Unemployment peaked in January 1994, when 16.6 percent of the workforce were jobless, but the NLE official said that this year unemployment could be even higher by June when Bulgaria is to introduce a tough fixed exchange rate mechanism, the currency board system.
Bulgaria's interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski told the national television on Monday some 58,000 people in the public sector would be laid off in the transitional period.

Hit by a severe economic crisis, Bulgaria has earmarked 64 loss-making state enterprises for closure. Restructuring at some of those firms had left some 22,000 people jobless in the last quarter of 1996, NLE figures showed.
Bulgaria's average unemployment rate for 1996 was 11.1 percent, down 0.3 points from 1995. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
